parameters.jsCode: const body=$input.first().json.body;const required=['dataset_name','data'];const missing=required.filter(f=>!body[f]);if(missing.length)return[{json:{valid:false,error:'Missing: '+missing.join(', ')}}];const data=Array.isArray(body.data)?body.data:[];if(data.length===0)return[{json:{valid:false,error:'data must be a non-empty array'}}];if(data.length>500)return[{json:{valid:false,error:'data exceeds 500 row limit'}}];const rows=data.slice(0,500);const keys=Object.keys(rows[0]||{});const sample=rows.slice(0,5);const stats={};keys.forEach(k=>{const vals=rows.map(r=>r[k]).filter(v=>v!==null&&v!==undefined&&v!=='');const nums=vals.map(v=>parseFloat(v)).filter(n=>!isNaN(n));stats[k]={totalRows:rows.length,nullCount:rows.length-vals.length,uniqueCount:new Set(vals.map(String)).size,isNumeric:nums.length>vals.length*0.8,min:nums.length?Math.min(...nums):null,max:nums.length?Math.max(...nums):null,mean:nums.length?parseFloat((nums.reduce((a,b)=>a+b,0)/nums.length).toFixed(4)):null,sampleValues:vals.slice(0,5).map(String)};if(nums.length>1){const mean=stats[k].mean;const variance=nums.reduce((a,b)=>a+Math.pow(b-mean,2),0)/nums.length;stats[k].stddev=parseFloat(Math.sqrt(variance).toFixed(4));}});return[{json:{valid:true,datasetName:body.dataset_name.trim(),dataDescription:(body.data_description||'').slice(0,400),expectedPatterns:(body.expected_patterns||'').slice(0,400),knownIssues:(body.known_issues||'').slice(0,300),rowCount:rows.length,columns:keys,columnStats:stats,sampleRows:sample,rawData:rows,replyEmail:body.reply_email||null}}];

values.content: You detect anomalies in datasets. You analyze column statistics, identify suspicious values, flag data quality issues, and give specific actionable findings — not generic advice. You distinguish between anomalies (statistically unusual values that might be real), errors (values that are almost certainly wrong), and data quality issues (missing data, format inconsistencies, duplicates). Always respond in valid JSON only.
